items.title: After Years of Disruption, an LRT Train Is Finally Set to Roll Down Topflight Drive
items.summary: According to INsauga, Ontario Transportation Minister Prabmeet Sarkaria announced Friday that a Hazel McCallion Line light rail vehicle is set to begin testing on Topflight Drive in Mississauga next week, following years of construction, delays and road disruptions tied to the project. Sarkaria shared the update in a post on X, saying progress continues on the line, though he did not offer further details on how long the testing would run or how far the train would travel. INsauga reports the significance of this round of testing is that it will happen on the actual LRT corridor itself, rather than being confined to the project's operations, maintenance and storage facility near Highway 407. That facility was the site of an earlier milestone, when Metrolinx said in June that the outdoor rail yard's overhead catenary system had been energized, allowing one of the project's light rail vehicles to operate under its own power for the first time. Metrolinx said at the time that achievement would pave the way for testing vehicles on the line itself, which now appears to be happening. For residents who have lived alongside years of construction along the corridor, next week's test marks one of the first visible signs of trains actually running on Mississauga streets.

items.title: House of the week: Upgraded home in family-friendly Mississauga neighbourhood
items.summary: This place: An upgraded home in a family-friendly Mississauga neighbourhood. Features: This upgraded home is located on a corner lot. A grand double-door entry opens to over 4,800 square feet of total living space that features hardwood floors throughout. The main level offers formal living and dining spaces, an office and a family room anchored by a fireplace. The custom kitchen features cabinets, granite countertops and a bright breakfast area overlooking the backyard. The home boasts five bedrooms, including two primary bedrooms. The primary bedrooms have walk-in closets and ensuite bathrooms. The additional bedrooms also have their own closets. The basement features a recreational space. Home updates include a metal roof with a 50-year warranty along with updated windows and window coverings throughout. This home is near Meadowvale Conservation Area, Lake Aquitaine Park, Churchill Meadows Community Centre, Lisgar GO Station and several golf courses. Thanks to Sam McDadi Real Estate Inc. Brokerage for all the information about the House of the Week. For more information about this house, please visit Sam McDadi Real Estate Inc.

items.title: Chase That Began Near Toronto's Esplanade Ends With Three Charged in Fatal Mississauga Shooting
items.summary: According to INsauga, Toronto police announced Thursday that three people, including 19-year-old Kahiem Bailey-Whitfield of Mississauga, are facing charges tied to the fatal officer-involved shooting that happened earlier this week near The Collegeway and Winston Churchill Boulevard. Also charged are 23-year-old Naquon Laidley of Toronto and a 17-year-old girl. Police say the case began when officers received a report of a person with a gun near The Esplanade and Lower Jarvis Street in Toronto, and officers from 51 Division identified a suspect vehicle that plainclothes officers then tracked all the way from Toronto into Mississauga. INsauga reports that when officers tried to stop the vehicle near The Collegeway and Winston Churchill Boulevard, the driver attempted to flee and struck a plainclothes officer in the process. What followed, including the shooting that left a man dead, remains under investigation by Ontario's Special Investigations Unit. Bailey-Whitfield now faces multiple firearms charges, including two counts each of possessing a restricted or prohibited firearm without a licence, occupying a motor vehicle with a firearm, possessing a loaded regulated firearm, and possessing a prohibited weapon without authority.

items.title: Port Credit's Waterfront Turns Into a Rib-Eating Marathon This Weekend, With a Midway Attached
items.summary: According to INsauga, Port Credit Ribfest X 2026 takes over Memorial Park from August 7 to 9, marking the second stop in Mississauga this summer for one of Ontario's biggest rib festivals. Produced by Ontario Festival Group and presented by Gelateria Italiana, the three-day event brings in some of North America's top pitmasters serving smoked ribs, pulled pork, brisket, barbecue chicken, smoked sausage and oversized beef “Dino” ribs. INsauga reports the food lineup extends well beyond barbecue, with vendors including Alabama Lemonade, Billy Bob's Bloomin' Onions, Pineapple Queen, Ontario Corn Roasters and BeaverTails rounding out the offerings alongside poutine, roasted corn and other festival staples. Beyond the food, organizers have built out a full weekend of entertainment and activities, including live music, an artisan marketplace, carnival games, a midway, face painting and a dedicated Kids Zone. The entertainment schedule mixes tribute acts with local bands throughout the weekend, and Friday's lineup features Ida-Maria, Dingo, Pink Leather Jackets and Fiddlestix. For anyone looking to spend a summer weekend on the Port Credit waterfront, the festival offers a packed schedule of food and live entertainment through Sunday.

items.title: Overcrowded Mississauga animal shelter cuts adoption fees for dogs and cats
items.summary: Mississauga Animal Services is asking residents to consider opening their homes to a shelter pet as overcrowding forces the city to launch a special adoption event. The shelter has reached capacity for dogs, and officials say every adoption will help create space for other animals in need of care. From Aug. 8 to Aug. 22, residents can adopt any dog or cat at Mississauga Animal Services for $25, plus HST and any applicable pet licensing fees. The reduced adoption fee is a significant discount from the shelter’s regular rates, which are typically $280 plus HST for dogs and puppies and up to $190 plus HST for cats and kittens. The Homeward Bound adoption event is open to anyone looking to add a pet to their family. No appointment is required, although wait times may vary. Adopters must be at least 18 years old. “Every adoption helps create space for other animals in need,” the city said. All animals available through Mississauga Animal Services receive basic medical care before adoption, including vaccinations and spay or neuter surgery, helping reduce some of the initial costs that come with bringing a new pet home. Shelter staff can also provide guidance for first-time pet owners, including advice on training, food, exercise and helping a new animal adjust to its surroundings.

items.title: Mississauga launches review of data centres, plans temporary development halt
items.summary: Mississauga council has approved a motion to temporarily halt approvals for new data centres while the city reviews its planning policies for the rapidly expanding sector. The motion directs staff to prepare an interim control bylaw (ICBL) that, if approved by council on Sept. 16, would prohibit approvals for data centres and other digital infrastructure projects for up to one year under Ontario’s Planning Act. A temporary pause would allow the city to complete a comprehensive review of the planning implications of data centres and determine whether changes are needed to its Official Plan and zoning bylaw. The review will examine the impact of data centres on municipal infrastructure, economic activity, the environment, noise, and energy and water consumption. It will also consider the role of the provincial and federal governments in regulating the sector and include opportunities for public consultation. Data centres are secure facilities that house computer servers used to store and process digital information for services including banking, health care, business operations, cloud computing and artificial intelligence applications. Mississauga has received a rezoning application to permit a data centre in the Meadowvale Business Park. Data centres are currently permitted in designated employment areas, where they are classified as warehousing, distribution and wholesaling under the Official Plan and as warehouse/distribution or science and technology facilities under the zoning bylaw. Several data centres already operate in the city. Staff said the review will consider whether the existing planning classifications remain appropriate as larger facilities are proposed. Staff will present the proposed interim control bylaw to council on Sept. 16. If approved, new data centre development would be prohibited until the bylaw expires.

items.title: The inside story of how the investigation into the murder of a Mississauga mother hit a dead end
items.summary: The three years that lapsed between when Mezhgan Aini went missing to when she was reported missing to police was a major impediment to finding the evidence needed to lay charges, police said. Mezhgan Aini, 38, was last seen in June 2022, police said in a news release issued on Monday. Aini, who also went by “Sara” or “Sarah,” was reported missing to Peel police in June 2025 by family who are overseas. Peel police have informed the family of a mother of three who disappeared from her Mississauga home four years ago that they have suspended the probe into her murder. Police told the Star that the three years that lapsed between when she went missing to when she was reported missing to police was a major impediment to finding the evidence needed to lay charges. The Star obtained a note the lead investigator sent to the family of Mezhgan Aini on June 29, informing them police had “exhausted all investigative leads,” and were pausing the investigation. “That is not to say it will never be looked at again, it means that we are not actively investigating it, however if new leads or information is learned, we will investigate it,” Det. Kevin Robbie told the family in an email. Mezhgan, 38, was last seen in June 2022 in the vicinity of her Mississauga apartment where she lived with her husband, Mohammad Yama Aini, and three children, now ages nine, 14 and 17, police said. She was not reported missing by her husband or children.
